sonnet.problem: The question quotes Paul's "running in vain" and then asks what he's worried about. The right answer, "That his work was for nothing", is just "in vain" reworded, so the question holds its own answer. It is also not an informed guess, since the baker has nothing to reason from.
sonnet.rule: A choice card's question never holds its own answer, or a form of it, like "rock badgers" for "in the rocks." Ask something else.

sonnet.problem: The question says the false brothers "spied on their freedom in Christ Jesus". That is the right answer to card 10, so the answer shown on card 10 is used again on card 11.
sonnet.rule: An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: The joke "I get nervous when the oven TIMER looks at me" doesn't match the core action. Paul is unimpressed by the leaders' status, and Dorin is nervous about a timer. A stranger would say "huh?"
sonnet.rule: The everyday comparison must have the same action. ... If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

sonnet.problem: The joke compares Paul next to Peter with Dorin next to the shiny new stamper "and NOBODY does that". The action doesn't match, because Paul and Peter are entrusted with the same work. It also leans on backstory the baker may not know, and it is unclear.
sonnet.rule: The everyday comparison must have the same action. ... It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.
